findings.finding: Existing stall test passes all five checks while using a pitch-command controller and promptly commanding recovery. It cannot validate prolonged stalls or pilot control effectiveness.

24 scripted native cases completed with finite states and eventual alpha below10deg. This is neither settled-recovery acceptance nor aircraft fidelity. A 950lb, brakes-closed, 10s held-input case reaches a -64.63deg flight path while nose attitude is within10deg of level; overall minimum flight path is -74.12deg. This includes a secondary stall after a steep climb caused by held aft input. The -64.63deg near-level sample occurs at45.208s after the script has returned to its original fixed trim, not while forward input is being held. Scripted recovery is intentionally not a competent closed-loop pilot; these excursions alone do not prove erroneous aerodynamics.

Same case at120/240/480Hz retains severe transients; overall minimum flight paths -74.12/-73.88/-73.82deg. Alpha drops below10deg3.59/3.58/3.57s after forward command. This argues against a simple native timestep artifact in this isolated case; it does not exonerate the product input/wind/frame path.

Native control sweep confirms full nose-up trim cancels full forward elevator command to neutral surface because pitch trim and stick are added and clipped. Correct SGS bungee/ratchet trim, stick travel and force interpretation need definition; incident trim unknown. Default reference trim is only0.10626088.

Estimated CL falls from1.76 at16.33deg to1.0 at20.63deg and0.21 at34.38deg. Pitch/yaw/roll stability derivatives and inertia are inherited approximations; no measured SGS post-stall/recovery validation. This shape is a suspect, not a proven root cause.

Dual manual calibration points match by construction. Independent solo45mph point is24.172:1 versus23:1 (+5.096%, outside declared5% tolerance); solo38mph sink2.505fps versus2.6fps. Historical manual speeds treated as CAS with assumed780/1040lb loads; these are not measured validation data for this airframe.

SoaringAudio varies generic airflow with airspeed but does not implement an AoA-dependent pre-stall buffet cue. Legacy stall fields are not updated from native SGS data. Any cue must reflect the modeled buffet envelope, not invent a horn or move the OpenXR camera.

Differential-airflow section forces use a tanh lift approximation without the native post-stall drop. Must compare native baseline plus incremental wind/wake forces around stall before changing either. No proof this caused the headset event.

references.scope: Historical manufacturer scan, pages1-5 through1-7: gentle straight-ahead stalls, pre-stall buffet, reference performance. Scan caveat and revision limitations apply; not current operating guidance.
Type-support source lists revised SFM dated2022-02-15 available to order. Current applicable full manual not obtained.
Page2 identifies NACA43012A application but expressly warns tested model shape differs from true airfoil; RC Reynolds numbers. Reject as direct full-scale SGS polar calibration.

repairSequence.task: Capture an exact diagnostic replay through existing native-step events: raw stick/grab ownership, applied elevator and trim, actual surface, AoA, beta, TAS/CAS, attitude, body rates, force/moment, airbrake, wind/wake, assistance, focus and simulation backlog. Bounded pre/post-event buffer, modest sampling; no per-step disk writes or simulation time loss.
repairSequence.acceptance: Show where commanded versus applied input first differs; replay separately through native-only and full product path.

repairSequence.task: Define SGS control semantics from the modeled trim system; fix the full-travel/trim relationship if it violates the documented mechanism. Preserve C172 mapping and all SGS mechanical deflection limits.
repairSequence.acceptance: Native control sweep at all trim settings, signs/endpoints/monotonicity/release ownership; show actual forward elevator during stall recovery. No guessed trim-force coefficients labeled real.

repairSequence.task: Replace unsupported SGS lift/drag/pitch schedules only against sourced geometry, mass/inertia/CG and credible aerodynamic evidence; preserve a separate SGS model on native JSBSim. Model wing washout, tail/elevator authority, downwash and stall progression consistently.
repairSequence.acceptance: Review coefficient continuity, positive dissipative drag, correct frame/moment signs and stability across permitted CG; label estimates and uncertainty. No forced nose-drop, velocity clamp, hidden lift or autopilot rescue.

repairSequence.task: Validate the complete reference envelope, not two calibration points: clean/braked polar, solo/dual and permitted CG/weight extremes, trim speeds, longitudinal response, roll rate/adverse yaw/rudder/slips, slow/accelerated/turning stalls, prolonged stall and unloading recovery.
repairSequence.acceptance: Independent reference points and declared tolerances before fitting; separate repeatability, qualitative handling and measured aircraft matching. No spin-fidelity claim without spin data.

repairSequence.task: Integrate and test atmosphere/wake gradients and post-release operation with the validated native response; add aircraft-appropriate pre-stall cues through authored audio/haptics.
repairSequence.acceptance: Still-air zero-increment invariant; no double-counted lift; bounded continuous forces; cue onset corresponds to reference/model; tracked camera never written.

repairSequence.task: Run native scenarios, C172 unchanged regression, tow/release/soaring/landing/training scenarios, visual QA and Android build; preserve APK/source/model hashes and compare final actual Quest behavior.
repairSequence.acceptance: All scoped software gates plus independent real SGS pilot/instructor handling review and actual focused Quest timing. Existing72Hz performance failure and other acceptance failures remain separate.

decision: Do not retune aerodynamic coefficients or publish a supposedly realistic fix from this evidence. New work this turn is diagnostic tooling and status/evidence only. No defect fix or replacement APK is claimed.
